summary: Remote-controlled daemon: WebSocket gateway drives local process/PTY execution
details: The package ships a `whalent` daemon (bin -> dist/index.cjs) that connects to a WebSocket gateway (default vendor-controlled at wss://…/gw/sdk/ws, overridable via --gateway) and, per its README, accepts remote commands (upgrade, restart) from that gateway and auto-starts/orchestrates worker processes on the host. Dependencies include ws, ssh2, @xterm/headless, and optional node-pty — a stack that supports interactive shell/PTY execution and SSH driven by remote messages. Both dist/index.cjs (~158 KB) and dist/core.cjs (~14 MB) are heavily obfuscated with javascript-obfuscator (string-array + rotate + hex identifiers, declared in devDependencies), so the exact network→exec dataflow inside the daemon's command handler cannot be audited from the shipped bundle. A network-sourced command channel that drives local child_process / PTY / SSH execution on the installer's host is a backdoor shape regardless of the advertised purpose, and the obfuscation of the command-dispatch code path removes any transparency about what the gateway is allowed to invoke locally.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
